title: Add structured request/response logging middleware
description: Introduce a built‑in logger that records incoming requests and outgoing responses in a structured JSON format. This gives developers real‑time visibility into traffic, aids debugging, and supports integration with log aggregation services.
testCases: Verify that a GET request logs method, url, status, response time, and optional request ID in JSON to the configured output
Verify that logger can be disabled via configuration and that disabling does not affect request handling or response times
acceptance: When the logger is enabled, each request results in a single JSON line written to the console (or configured stream) containing method, url, status code, response time, and a unique request ID. The logger can be toggled off via a config flag without throwing errors or altering response payloads. All existing tests continue to pass.
reason: Production systems need reliable observability. A zero‑dependency, configurable logger aligns with yantraverse’s lightweight ethos while solving a common operational pain point, improving debugging speed and enabling seamless integration with monitoring pipelines.
